nodes.label: Choose the Narrowest Reference File
nodes.rationale: The index exists so an agent loads only the smallest reference that fits the current task, keeping context focused instead of pulling the whole skill corpus; each entry carries a priority (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM) and an explicit authority source so precedence between overlapping references is decidable.

nodes.label: Objective Launch Verification Evidence
nodes.rationale: A spawned process is not proof the app works, so verification demands objective signals (non-zero main window handle, expected window title, responsive process with a visible shell, no immediate startup exception). The verified final instance is deliberately left running so the user can see the working app rather than take the agent's word for it.

nodes.label: Explicit x64 Platform Target for Local Verification
nodes.rationale: WinUI output is sensitive to architecture defaults, so AnyCPU can produce ambiguous or unlaunchable output; pinning x64 removes that ambiguity during local verification.
nodes.norm_label: explicit x64 platform target for local verification

nodes.label: Platform Controls First Before Toolkit Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Toolkit packages are added only for a verified gap, because convenience-driven dependencies hide fundamental UX problems, inflate the package set for minor visual differences, and must be justified in writing against the rejected built-in alternative.
nodes.norm_label: platform controls first before toolkit dependencies

nodes.label: Built-In WinUI Controls First
nodes.rationale: Replacing standard controls purely to change appearance costs platform behavior (accessibility, input, theming) that the built-in control already provides for free.

nodes.label: CommandBar as Native Command Surface
nodes.rationale: A stock CommandBar with its overflow model covers grouped document, formatting, view, and page-level actions; hand-built toolbar rows from Grid/StackPanel/Border only pay off against a verified CommandBar limitation or explicit design requirement.

nodes.label: Single Search Field with Live Filtering
nodes.rationale: Explicit apply/refresh/mode controls only earn their place when the underlying operation is expensive, remote, asynchronous, or semantically different; for local filtering they are redundant chrome.
nodes.norm_label: single search field with live filtering

nodes.label: Explicit Adaptive Breakpoint Intent
nodes.rationale: Breakpoints are defined by answering when a shelf becomes a stacked list, when a footer drops nonessential controls, and when the page stops being a desktop canvas; effective pixels replace fixed device assumptions.

nodes.label: Remove Redundant Outer Section Borders
nodes.rationale: Fewer layers adapt more cleanly across breakpoints, so redundant surfaces are removed before more adaptive layout rules are added.

nodes.label: Setup-and-Scaffold Flow (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Setup instructions live in one place (SKILL.md plus the bundled config.yaml WinGet bootstrap) so references never paraphrase or fork the install workflow; duplicated setup recipes drift and produce ad hoc per-component installs.

nodes.label: Manual Non-Mutating Readiness Audit
nodes.rationale: The bundled bootstrap can change the machine, so an audit-only request gets consent first or falls back to read-only checks reported under present / missing / uncertain / recommended-optional headings, keeping uncertainty distinct from confirmed absence.

nodes.label: Packaged App by Default
nodes.rationale: Packaged is the smoothest first-project, F5, deployment, and Store-compatible path and gives package identity plus package-backed APIs; unpackaged is chosen only when the user needs repeatable CLI build-and-run verification, direct .exe launches, an installer, or existing desktop integration. The choice must be made before startup, storage, and launch code are written, because deferring it forces a later conversion.

nodes.label: Standard Blank App Template First
nodes.rationale: Scaffolding through the official template and layering navigation, title bar, and windowing later keeps the app rooted in a known-good shape; copying prebuilt baseline files instead removes the diffable reference used during recovery.

nodes.label: Template-First Recovery for Startup and XAML Failures
nodes.norm_label: template-first recovery for startup and xaml failures

nodes.label: Template-First Recovery Loop
nodes.rationale: Recovery diffs only the startup and shared-resource surface against a matching-packaging comparison scaffold, then reverts toward the template shape, because swapping in alternate baseline files or flattening styles inline destroys the reference point and turns an opaque failure into a permanent structural change.

nodes.label: Opaque MSB3073 / XamlCompiler.exe Failures
nodes.rationale: MSB3073 is not proof that the most recently edited XAML line is at fault; the failure may live in app code, shared resources, or project structure, which is why isolation precedes edits.

nodes.label: Avoid Window.Current in WinUI 3 Startup
nodes.rationale: WinUI 3 startup should use an explicit new Window(); Window.Current is a UWP-era pattern that misbehaves in desktop WinUI 3 startup code.

nodes.label: Centralized Shared Resource Dictionaries
nodes.rationale: App-wide theme resources and styles live in App.xaml and shared dictionaries because scattering brushes across page-local dictionaries makes theming inconsistent and untraceable.

nodes.label: x:Bind vs Binding Guidance
nodes.rationale: x:Bind gives compile-time safety and performance for page-local properties and typed view models; classic Binding is reserved for dynamic data contexts and flexible templates. MVVM ceremony beyond what the project will maintain is explicitly discouraged.
nodes.community_name: Windows App SDK Lifecycle, Notifications, and Deployment

nodes.label: Built-In Transitions Before Custom Animation Systems
nodes.rationale: Motion must clarify hierarchy, continuity, and state; decorative animation delays interaction, overlapping animations muddle a single state change, and animation must never hide focus, selection, or accessibility state. Toolkit animation helpers are a last resort.
nodes.norm_label: built-in transitions before custom animation systems

nodes.label: Keep the UI Thread Free
nodes.rationale: Layout, rendering, and input all contend for the UI thread, so expensive I/O or CPU work is deferred or backgrounded; slow-frame findings are read as UI-thread overload rather than a cue for blind micro-optimization.

nodes.label: Measurement Before Optimization
nodes.rationale: Guessing at performance causes wastes effort and can make layout worse; profiling data must exist before a performance claim or fix is asserted.

nodes.label: Simpler Visual Trees and Lighter Templates
nodes.norm_label: simpler visual trees and lighter templates

nodes.label: Canonical Source Preference Order
nodes.rationale: Learn is authoritative for requirements and behavior, WinUI Gallery for concrete control usage and shell composition, WindowsAppSDK-Samples for scenario APIs and platform integration, and CommunityToolkit only when Toolkit-specific functionality is genuinely required. Each task row also names a backup source so lookups degrade gracefully.

nodes.label: WinUI Gallery (microsoft/WinUI-Gallery)
nodes.community_name: Windows App SDK Lifecycle, Notifications, and Deployment

nodes.label: NavigationView as Functional Shell Chrome
nodes.rationale: The nav pane is chrome first: overloading it with every command, or turning it into a branded hero area with logos and taglines, breaks the shell's native feel. Left nav suits several stable destinations, top nav suits few peers with spare width, and shallow workflows should stay document-first.

nodes.label: Custom Title Bar as Functional Chrome
nodes.rationale: Title bar customization must preserve drag regions, caption button clarity, and light/dark/high-contrast states; branding is secondary to behaving like a Windows title bar.
nodes.norm_label: custom title bar as functional chrome

nodes.label: AppWindow and Windows App SDK Windowing
nodes.rationale: Start with one main window and add secondary windows only for document detachment, inspection panes, or tool windows; use the Windowing samples rather than inventing custom platform abstractions for resize and placement.
nodes.norm_label: appwindow and windows app sdk windowing

nodes.label: Narrow/Phone-Width Navigation Mode
nodes.rationale: At phone-like widths a permanent desktop pane steals the content column, so the shell switches to minimal or overlay mode, shows the pane toggle, closes the pane after navigation, and reduces padding and decorative chrome.

nodes.label: Theme Resources Over Hard-Coded Colors
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded light-theme colors break dark and high-contrast modes; centralizing brushes, typography, and corner/spacing tokens in shared dictionaries keeps all three themes correct by construction.

nodes.label: Acrylic for Transient Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Acrylic belongs on flyouts, menus, and other light-dismiss surfaces; using it where Mica or a plain theme-aware surface would do is more expensive and less clear.

nodes.label: Card-Around-Cards Border Anti-Pattern
nodes.rationale: An outer section Border around content already grouped by card controls, spacing, or headers adds a redundant surface layer; system resources such as CardBackgroundFillColorDefaultBrush and LayerFillColorDefaultBrush should carry grouping instead of a parallel bespoke surface language.

nodes.label: Fluent Typography and Iconography
nodes.rationale: Typography creates hierarchy so extra borders and decoration are unnecessary; Segoe UI Variable and standard Windows icons with consistent visual weight keep the app reading as native.

nodes.label: Restrained Tag and Chip Treatments
nodes.rationale: Rows of bright oval pills for routine metadata are visual noise; small rounded rectangles or subtle badges are the default when a metadata container is justified at all.

nodes.label: Required Verification Loop
nodes.rationale: Build after each meaningful edit rather than only at the end, and verify actual launch instead of inferring success from a spawned process, so failures are attributed to the edit that caused them.

nodes.label: Hot Reload, Live Visual Tree, and Live Property Explorer
nodes.rationale: When a collection page looks wrong, the live tree is inspected for nested ScrollViewer ownership before the item template is rewritten, because the bug is often layout ownership rather than card markup.
nodes.norm_label: hot reload, live visual tree, and live property explorer

nodes.label: Runtime Verification at Multiple Breakpoints
nodes.rationale: XAML structure alone does not prove resize behavior; wide, medium, and phone-width states plus theme and input-mode changes are reproduced against the running app before an issue is called fixed.
